keyTerms.definition: The complete correct response each key entry gives.
A wrong-answer pattern the key warns against.
Point breakdown per question.

recall.question: What does each key entry provide?
recall.answer: Strong answers, red flags, and rubrics.

keyTerms.definition: grad_x log p: the gradient kills the additive normalizer.
Become tractable to fit without partition functions.

recall.question: Why does the score not need the partition function, and what does that buy?
recall.answer: The score is grad_x log p. The normalizer is additive in log space, so the gradient kills it. This buys training without partition functions: energy models become tractable to fit.

keyTerms.definition: div s_theta from integration by parts.
Turns E[s_theta·s] into -E[div s_theta].

recall.question: Derive the explicit score-matching objective and name the trace.
recall.answer: Expand E[0.5||s_theta - s||²]. Cross term E[s_theta·s] = -E[div s_theta] by parts. Drop constants. The trace is div s_theta, the divergence of the model field.

keyTerms.definition: Posterior mean by construction; under a bimodal posterior it sits between modes.
Where the mean sits between modes: why it is not a sample.

recall.question: State Tweedie's formula and explain why it is not a sample.
recall.answer: E[x_0|x] = x + sigma² grad_x log p(x). It is a posterior mean by construction (Bayes + Gaussian noise). A mean is not a sample: under a bimodal posterior it sits between modes.

keyTerms.definition: q(x_t|x_0) Gaussian in closed form: any t is O(1).
Any t costs O(1); simulating the chain costs O(t).

recall.question: Why does DDPM training sample t uniformly instead of simulating the chain?
recall.answer: q(x_t|x_0) is Gaussian in closed form, so any t is O(1) to sample. Simulating the chain would cost O(t) per sample and teach nothing extra.

keyTerms.definition: In [0,1]: 0 is the deterministic ODE, 1 is DDPM.
Keeps marginals only approximately: colors shift, details wash out.

recall.question: What does eta control, and what breaks under aggressive striding?
recall.answer: Eta in [0,1] sets the noise per reverse step: 0 is the deterministic ODE, 1 is DDPM. Striding keeps marginals only approximately: too aggressive and colors shift, details wash out.

keyTerms.definition: 2x calls per step: conditional plus unconditional.
w=3 too large when samples show saturation, distortion.

recall.question: Why does classifier-free guidance double the sampling cost, and when is w=3 too large?
recall.answer: Each step evaluates both the conditional and the unconditional score: 2x calls. w = 3 is too large when samples show overshoot artifacts (saturation, distortion): fidelity up, diversity and realism down.

keyTerms.definition: Toy x_4 = 1.5174; reverse kernel mean 1.8983, variance 0.0714.
Same step: DDIM 1.7630 deterministic; DDPM mean 1.8983 plus noise.

recall.question: A sampler with 4 DDIM steps looks washed out. Diagnose and fix.
recall.answer: Striding broke the marginal match. Fix: add steps back until quality recovers, or switch to a higher-order solver. Measure quality versus steps.

keyTerms.definition: dx = -0.5 beta(t) x dt + sqrt(beta(t)) dw.
dx = [f - 0.5 g² score] dt: same marginals, no noise.
Score must exist and be smooth at all t; manifold data has none at t=0.

recall.question: Compute the boundary score for the smoothed uniform.
recall.answer: Smoothed uniform sigma = 0.05: score 13.5 at x = 0.01, 0.0 inside.

recall.question: Why does the ODE likelihood need a named noise floor?
recall.answer: The likelihood integrates the smoothed law; the noise floor is a free parameter that moves the number. Name it or the comparison is void.

keyTerms.definition: Differentiate log p(x) under the integral; derivative brings down (x_0-x)/sigma².
N(x;x_0,sigma^2): what lets you differentiate under the integral.

recall.question: Prove Tweedie's formula for Gaussian noise.
recall.answer: p(x_0|x) proportional to N(x;x_0,sigma²)p(x_0). Write the posterior mean as an integral. Differentiate log p(x) under the integral: the derivative brings down (x_0-x)/sigma². Rearrange to (E[x_0|x]-x)/sigma².

keyTerms.definition: Base N(0,I); exact eps reconstructs the forward marginal at t-1.
Makes x0_hat = x_0: the inductive step's key.

recall.question: Show the DDIM eta=0 update preserves the DDPM marginals.
recall.answer: Base: at t=T both are N(0,I) by construction. Inductive step: assume x_t marginal matches. The DDIM eta=0 update is x_{t-1} = sqrt(alpha_bar_{t-1})x0_hat + sqrt(1-alpha_bar_{t-1})eps_pred. With the true eps, x0_hat = x_0 exactly and the update reconstructs the forward marginal at t-1.

keyTerms.definition: Tweedie single-step test separates sampler from model.
Pure noise the model never saw: the third cause.

recall.question: Name three candidate causes with one test each, in order.
recall.answer: (1) Sampler/schedule mismatch: sampling betas differ from training, or strided without DDIM. Test Tweedie single-step sharpness: sharp there but mushy after sampling proves the sampler. (2) Time embedding present but broken: test loss per t; flat across t is the tell. (3) The loss 0.005 is on the training noise distribution but sampling starts from pure noise the model never saw at t=T: test the t=T marginal.

keyTerms.definition: DDIM 4 strided steps, distilled 4-step student, or consistency model.
Alternative 4-call sampler.

recall.question: Redesign the sampler for 4 network calls; state the cost and how you measure it.
recall.answer: DDIM with 4 strided steps, or a distilled 4-step student, or a consistency model. Cost: marginal mismatch. Measure a distributional distance to the 1000-step sampler at matched seeds plus human sharpness ratings. Report quality versus steps.

keyTerms.definition: Masking or uniform resampling; score becomes probability ratios.
What the score becomes on discrete sets.

recall.question: Redesign diffusion for discrete tokens; name which concepts break.
recall.answer: Discrete diffusion with masking or uniform resampling over the vocabulary. The score becomes probability ratios. Breaks: C01 (no gradient on discrete sets), C03 Tweedie, C09 SDE, C11 ODE solvers. Survives: chains, the loss shape, striding.

keyTerms.definition: Free parameter that can flip ODE-likelihood rankings.
Report likelihood with it: part of the fair experiment.

recall.question: Attack 'our model has the best ODE likelihood, so it is the best generative model' and propose the fair experiment.
recall.answer: Attack 1: the ODE likelihood needs a noise floor on discrete/bounded data; the ranking can flip with it. Attack 2: likelihood is one projection; best generative model needs samples, coverage, and cost. Fair experiment: fixed dequantization, likelihood with seed uncertainty, paired with precision/recall and sampling cost at matched budgets.
